svg.text: GP-11 Onion peeling: three slits and a dry wipe
Cut depth decides what comes off; three slits make segments with no undercut, so even a rough wipe removes them.
onion Ø 40–90 mm · 3 slits × 2.5 mm, re-pass 5 mm
spin 60–120 rpm · wipe 5 s dry, jet 3 s at 3 bar
25–30 s per onion (45 s with re-pass)
SIDE VIEW — onion on the spit (4 px per mm)
deep waste pan (skins never touch the cell)

g.text: V-nest
top cut: face = 0.7 D (10 mm)
tail cut: 0.6 D (7 mm)
blade with depth shoe: blade 2.5 mm proud, shoe rides at 3–5 N
onion turns 120° between slits
dry silicone finger comb (fixed)
fan jet 3 bar, 3 s
camera: neck tuft + root beard give the axis
camera check: skin = dull brown, flesh = glossy white
camera reads the cut face: dark centre → cut 4 mm more
20 mm

svg.text: END VIEW — section across the onion (skins drawn thicker)

g.text: fleshy scales
blade + shoe
3 slits at 120° → 3 segments of ≤ 180°:
no undercut, they fall off radially

svg.text: fleshy scale → it stays a closed

g.text: 1/7 Camera finds the axis (neck tuft, root beard); the onion lies in a V-nest.
2/7 Top cut where the face is 0.7 D; the camera reads the rings — a dark centre means cut 4 mm more.
3/7 Tail cut at 0.6 D: the outer scales are freed from the root plate; the core of the plate keeps the rest together.
4/7 Prong cups chuck the two cut faces (20–30 N); the nest drops away.
5/7 Three slits at 120°: the shoe flattens loose skin, the blade cuts exactly 2.5 mm deep.
6/7 Dry wipe: the onion spins against the silicone comb; the three skin segments fall off.
7/7 Fan jet 3 s, then camera check. Skin left > 5 % → second pass: 3 slits at 5 mm, offset 60°.
